one_liner: Freshdesk has a broad REST v2 API using an agent API key via Basic auth, but the free plan has no API access, so builders need a trial or paid plan.
auth_notes: Per-agent API key from Profile Settings, sent as the Basic Auth username with "X" as the password. Username/password auth has been phased out. A third-party guide describes an OAuth flow, but the official evidence only shows OAuth for Marketplace apps, so I did not rely on it.
access_notes: The Free plan and legacy Sprout plan have no API. Trials have API access at 50 calls/min. Paid plans (Growth, Pro, Enterprise) get 100/400/700 calls/min. Trial length is not stated in the evidence.
blocker_notes: The API is unavailable on the free plan. A builder must use a limited trial (50 calls/min) or buy a paid plan to get a working key.

evidence.quote: The Freshdesk API uses Basic Auth against your own subdomain, with the API key as the username and the letter X as the password.
An API key is a unique alphanumeric identifier, for each agent on your Freshdesk Account.
The Freshdesk Free plan doesn’t include API access, so the integration won’t work with it.
Freshdesk trial accounts have limited API access (50 calls per minute).

Freshdesk's APIs belong to the **Representational State Transfer (REST)** category. They allow you to perform 'RESTful' operations such as reading, modifying, adding or deleting data from your helpdesk.
The Freshworks Model Context Protocol (MCP) server enables AI tools like Cursor and Claude to securely connect and interact with Freshdesk.
